Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a truly overwhelming and life-changing experience. It's completely normal to have a mix of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you in any way I can.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there's anything we can do to support you during this postpartum period. The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us a better understanding of your emotional well-being right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and is a safe space for you to express yourself honestly. I'm here to listen and support you, not to judge. Our conversation will be guided by 10 questions that will help me understand your feelings and experiences over the past week.

We'll take this one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and supportive as possible. So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a bit down or overwhelmed?

(sighing) Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired all the time. I mean, I'm happy to have my baby, but it's just been so hard to adjust to this new life. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days, trying to take care of the baby and the house, but I don't really feel like myself anymore. I used to enjoy simple things like reading or taking a walk, but now I just don't have the energy or the interest. Even things that I thought would bring me joy, like spending time with my baby, feel like a chore sometimes. I just feel so sad and discouraged, like I'm not doing anything right. And the anxiety... it's constant. I worry about the baby's safety all the time, and it's hard to calm myself down when those thoughts start racing. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm not a good mom, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with. (fighting back tears) Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) Not really, to be honest. I mean, I used to be able to laugh and find the humor in things, but lately, it's been really hard for me to do that. I feel like I'm just going through the motions and trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying life. Sometimes my partner will try to make a joke or lighten the mood, but it just doesn't seem funny to me. I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy, but deep down, I'm really struggling. (pausing, looking down) It's hard to explain, but it's like the things that used to bring me joy just don't have the same effect on me anymore. Even when I do manage to laugh or smile, it feels forced, like I'm just putting on a show for everyone else. (sighing) It's like the happiness is just out of reach for me right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll make plans to do something, like take the baby for a walk or meet a friend for coffee, but when the time comes, I just don't feel like doing it. I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, like the baby will cry or I'll forget something important, and it just feels like too much effort. Sometimes I'll even get anxious just thinking about leaving the house with the baby. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like the excitement and anticipation I used to feel about doing things has just been replaced with dread and worry. Even things that I used to love, like reading or taking a relaxing bath, just don't seem enjoyable to me right now. (looking down) I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to get through each day, rather than actually looking forward to things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yes, that's definitely been happening. I feel like I'm always wondering what I could have done differently, or what I did wrong. Like, if the baby is crying, I'll think "If only I had fed her sooner" or "If only I had burped her better". And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right as a mom, and it just feels like I'm failing all the time. (pausing, looking down) I'll even beat myself up over little things, like if the house is a mess or if I didn't get a chance to shower that day. It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself, and it's hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and inadequacy. (sighing) Sometimes I'll even think about how my partner or family members might be judging me, and that just adds to the feeling of self-blame. It's like I'm always waiting for someone to tell me that I'm not doing a good enough job, and that's a really hard feeling to live with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's been happening a lot. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she chokes on something? What if I forget to lock the door and someone gets in? What if I'm not producing enough milk? It's just these constant, nagging worries that I know are irrational, but I just can't shake them off. (biting lip) And it's not just during the day, it's at night too. I'll be lying in bed, trying to fall asleep, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios. I'll think about the baby's safety, or my own health, or just all these things that could go wrong. (taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like my mind is just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when I try to calm myself down, I just can't seem to relax. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's like I'm always on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be doing something normal, like taking a shower or feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of panic. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (taking a deep breath) It's like my body is just reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no real reason for it. I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling like this?" But I just can't calm down. (shaking head) It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it or how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll even feel like I'm going to hurt myself or the baby, but that's not something I would ever do. It's just this fleeting thought that pops into my head, and it's terrifying. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) It's like I'm losing control, and it's really frightening.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling overwhelmed) Yes, that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to be a good partner and friend... it all just feels like too much. (sighing) I'll be in the middle of doing one thing, and then I'll think about all the other things I need to do, and it just feels like it's all too much to handle. I'll feel anxious and stressed, and I just want to curl up and hide. (looking down, shaking head) I know I'm not alone, and that lots of moms feel this way, but it's hard to shake off the feeling that I'm just not doing enough. That I'm failing somehow. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Even when my partner tries to help, or my family offers to lend a hand, I just feel like I'm still shouldering all the responsibility. It's like, I'm the mom, and it's all up to me to keep everything together. (feeling tears well up) And some days, it just feels like too much to bear.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, rubbing eyes) Yes, that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be lying in bed, trying to fall asleep, but my mind just won't shut off. I'll think about all the things I need to do, or worry about the baby, or just feel overwhelmed by everything. (sighing) And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or stressed, and I won't be able to get back to sleep. It's like my brain is just constantly racing, and I don't know how to calm it down. (looking down, shaking head) I'll try to relax, I'll try to focus on my breathing, but it's just hard to quiet my mind. And when I don't get enough sleep, it just makes everything worse. I'll feel more irritable, more anxious, more overwhelmed. It's like I'm stuck in this vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break free. (pausing, feeling tears well up) Some nights, I'll just lie there, feeling so unhappy and alone, and I'll wonder how I'm going to get through the next day. (voice cracking) It's just really hard, you know.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump in throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I'll just feel this deep sadness, like a weight is crushing me. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, my old self. I miss being able to do things spontaneously, to go out with friends, to just be able to take a shower without having to worry about the baby. (sighing) And now, as a mom, I just feel like I'm not doing enough, like I'm failing somehow. I'll look at other moms, and they seem so put together, so confident, and I just feel like I'm just faking it, like I'm just pretending to be a good mom. (shaking head) It's hard to shake off the feeling that I'm just not good enough.

And the sadness... it's just so overwhelming sometimes. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll start crying, and I won't be able to stop. (wiping away tears) It's like my emotions are just so raw, so close to the surface, and it's hard to keep them from boiling over. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Some days, it feels like the sadness is just suffocating me, like I'm drowning in it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just burst into tears. I'll be feeding the baby, or trying to get her to sleep, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of frustration and sadness, and I'll start crying. (wiping away tears) Sometimes I'll be crying and I won't even know why, it's just like my body is releasing all this pent-up emotion. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just so overwhelmed by everything, and crying is the only way I can release it all.

And it's not just little tears, either. I mean, I've had full-on sobbing fits, where I'm just curled up on the floor, crying uncontrollably. (shaking head) It's embarrassing, because my partner will try to comfort me, and I'll just push him away, because I don't know how to explain what's wrong. (looking down) I just feel so lost and alone, like I'm the only one who's feeling this way. (voice cracking) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm not allowed to feel this way. Like, I'm a mom now, and I'm supposed to be happy and grateful, and I'm just not. (tears streaming down face) I'm just so sad, and I don't know how to make it stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I've had those thoughts. They're scary and overwhelming, and I don't know how to make them stop. (taking a deep breath) It's like, I'll be feeling so anxious and sad, and I'll just think to myself, "What's the point of all this? Why am I even here?" And then these thoughts will creep in, like, "Maybe it would be easier if I just wasn't here anymore." (shaking head) It's like, I know it's not a rational thought, but it's just there, lurking in the back of my mind.

(looking up, tears in eyes) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel so trapped and alone, and I don't know how to escape. And those thoughts, they just feel like a way out, you know? Like, a way to just make all the pain and sadness stop. (voice cracking) But at the same time, I know it's not what I really want. I want to be here for my baby, for my partner, for my family. I want to be happy and healthy, but I just don't know how to get there right now.

(looking down, feeling a mix of shame and fear) I'm scared to admit this, because I don't want anyone to think I'm crazy or that I'm a bad mom. But at the same time, I know I need to be honest, because I need help. I need someone to talk to, someone to help me work through these feelings and find a way out of this darkness. (pausing, taking a deep breath) So, yeah... those thoughts have occurred to me. And I'm scared, but I'm also hopeful that we can work through this together.

The patient is experiencing a range of symptoms that are concerning for postpartum depression, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety. They report feeling overwhelmed by daily responsibilities and are having difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood. The patient also reports having thoughts of self-harm, which is a significant safety concern. It's clear that the patient is struggling to adjust to their new role and is in need of support and guidance.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 30, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient states they can't laugh and see the funny side of things like they used to, and even when they do, it feels forced, indicating a significant decrease in ability to find humor, matching 'Not at all</sym>, <sym>the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong tendency to self-blame, with frequent thoughts of 'what I could have done differently' and feelings of guilt and inadequacy, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports experiencing overwhelming panic and scary thoughts, including fleeting thoughts of self-harm or harm to the baby, indicating a high level of distress and panic, matching 'Yes, quite a lot</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong feeling of being overwhelmed, with statements like 'everything is just piling up on me,' 'it all just feels like too much to handle,' and 'some days, it just feels like too much to bear.' This suggests that the patient hasn't been able to cope at all most of the time, aligning with the guideline option for a score of 3.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they experience difficulty sleeping due to unhappiness most of the time, as evidenced by phrases like 'that's been happening to me a lot lately' and 'it's like my brain is just constantly racing</sym>, <sym>The patient describes feeling sad or miserable 'a lot lately', with emotions being 'so raw' and 'overwhelming', indicating a high frequency and intensity of these feelings, matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient explicitly mentions having thoughts of self-harm, describing them as recurring and related to feelings of overwhelm, anxiety, and sadness, which aligns with the 'Yes, quite often' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and responses to the EPDS questionnaire suggest a high risk for postpartum depression. The patient's report of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, combined with their difficulty coping with daily responsibilities and thoughts of self-harm, are all consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 30 also indicates a high risk for depression. The presence of self-harm thoughts is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention and follow-up. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if they experience any further thoughts of self-harm
3. Develop a safety plan with the patient to ensure their safety and the safety of their baby
4. Provide patient with resources for postpartum depression support, such as support groups and online resources
5. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities, such as exercise and meditation, to help manage symptoms
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
